```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
                      fig.height = 4, dpi = 150)
```

The default `cellprograms` pipeline fits each cell type separately and only
then asks whether programs are shared. Two experimental (v0.2.0.9001)
extensions invert the ordering and factorize across cell types directly:

- **EB-CP** (`fit_eb_cp()` / `eb_cp_from_fit()`): a tensor-style greedy EBMF
  over the stacked cell-type x donor matrices. Each rank-1 component is a
  gene loading (`U`), a donor activity vector (`V`) shared across the cell
  types the component spans, and a cell-type loading vector (`W`). Components
  are accepted by a held-out z gate on a donor-synchronous split, so the
  number of components is selected by out-of-sample predictive evidence, not
  by a variance cutoff.
- **Block EBMF** (`fit_joint_block()` / `block_clusters()`): a shared-first
  flashier pass over the stacked expression matrix, followed by per-cell-type
  private passes on the residuals. `block_clusters()` collapses shared
  factors into gene-set clusters by loading overlap and returns donor
  activity per cluster.

This vignette runs both on a small simulated dataset and states the scope
caveats measured in the coordination benchmark (see `benchmarks/coordination/`
in the repository).

```{r simulate}
library(cellprograms)

sim <- simulate_pseudobulk(scenario = "mixed", n_samples = 60,
                           n_genes = 800, program_size = 40, seed = 1)
x <- as_cell_program_data(sim$pseudobulk)
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 10L, seed = 1)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
```

## EB-CP: greedy components with held-out selection

`eb_cp_from_fit()` runs EB-CP on the adjusted per-cell-type matrices of a
fitted `cell_program_fit`. If `strata` is not supplied, the donor-synchronous
train/held-out split is derived from the covariates used at fit time, so the
split respects the adjustment; pass `strata` explicitly when you want a
different stratification.

```{r ebcp}
cp <- eb_cp_from_fit(fit)
cp$n_components
cp$kept_heldout_z          # held-out z of each kept component
cp$trace_z                 # z trace including the first failed component
```

`eb_cp_programs()` turns components into program calls. Components spanning
>= `min_members` cell types at the membership threshold are flagged as
coordination programs; the rest are kept as private programs, flagged rather
than dropped.

```{r ebcp-programs}
pr <- eb_cp_programs(cp)
pr$programs
head(pr$activity[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])   # donor activity per coordination component
```

## Block EBMF: shared-first pass plus private residuals

`fit_joint_block()` stacks the per-cell-type matrices and fits shared factors
first, then per-cell-type private factors on the residuals.

```{r block}
bfit <- fit_joint_block(fit, level = "expression", order = "shared_first",
                        max_factors = 10L, seed = 1, verbose = 0L)
bfit$shared_fit$n_factors
bc <- block_clusters(bfit, mass_thresh = 0.1)
head(bc$clusters, 10)
```

Each row of `bc$clusters` is a gene-set cluster (a group of shared factors
with overlapping loadings); `bc$activity` holds donor activity per cluster.
The block-mass rule (`mass_thresh`) keeps clusters whose membership spreads
across at least two cell types.

## Scope caveats from the coordination benchmark

Both extensions trade robustness for directness, and the preregistered
coordination benchmark (`benchmarks/coordination/`, tag `prereg-coord-v1`)
quantifies where:

- **Block EBMF (`block_E`) is powerful but over-calls without calibration.**
  On null data the shared-first pass still returns factors whose loadings
  spread across blocks, and the block-mass rule alone called spurious shared
  programs in 16/16 null replicates. A permutation-calibrated significance
  layer (within-strata donor permutation, max-T family-wise control) is
  available in the benchmark harness and is being productized; until then,
  treat uncalibrated `block_clusters()` output as a candidate list, not as
  evidence of sharing.
- **EB-CP is conservative.** The held-out z gate keeps specificity high
  (near-zero false positives on null data) but loses power when shared
  programs have cell-type-specific gene loadings, because the model's shared
  donor-activity assumption is only approximately met.
- **Low-K regime.** Both methods were validated with few recurring programs
  (1-3) against many private ones. With dozens of true per-cell-type
  programs, set `max_factors` above the default and expect the shared-first
  ordering to matter more.

For the default-by-construction path (per-cell-type fits, then
`sharing_spectrum()` / `plot_sharing_spectrum()`), see
`vignette("quickstart")`.
